PROJECT NO. 58481

RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION §
STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561 § OF TEXAS

COMMENTS OF PROVIDENT, INC. ON STAFF’s
PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION OF NEW 16 TAC §25.194

COMES NOW Provident, Inc. (Provident) and files these comments regarding
Commission Staff’s Proposal for Publication (PFP) of new 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC)
§25.194 relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards, which would set forth the standards
and criteria for an electric utility to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission
network. The PFP will be considered by the Commission at its March 12, 2026, Open Meeting.
Provident has significant concerns with the Staff Proposal, as explained more fully below, and
respectfully requests that the Commission consider making changes to the PFP prior to voting to
publish proposed rules for comment pursuant to the Administrative Procedures Act.

Provident is a Texas-based U.S. developer of hyperscale data center campuses and powered
land, focused on delivering transmission-ready sites for investment-grade tenants. The company
has five active projects in ERCOT, primarily within the North Texas area, including 500 MW
secured under an executed facilities agreement that is currently under active construction,
supported by tens of millions in committed utility deposits and an additional 1.3 GW request
pending for nearly two years. Provident is also granting land rights and easements to enable
development of a new switching station that will strengthen regional grid reliability, and its
projects are reflected in multiple ERCOT Regional Transmission Plans and Regional Planning

Group activities.

 Provident’s vertical developments are backed by institutional capital, including Blackstone
and other major Texas-based investors. The company is active across multiple states — Texas,
Indiana, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Missouri, Mississippi, Kansas, and Alabama — and has
experience working under a wide range of utility frameworks, regulatory environments, and
interconnection processes.

Vertical development exceeds $4 billion across several campuses, with additional powered-
land projects exceeding $2 billion and more than 4 GW of capacity nationwide, positioning
Provident among the most active powered-land developers in the United States. Due to limited
interconnection progress in Texas over the past 2.5 years, the company has shifted substantial
development activity to other states.

Provident’ s model — acquiring raw land, securing entitlements, delivering powered shells,
and fully fitted out buildings — fills a critical role in the data center ecosystem. Hyperscale
customers typically prefer to lease facilities to preserve capital for IT infrastructure, which often
represents significantly larger investment than the real estate itself. Developers provide the upfront
land, permitting, power coordination, and building delivery needed to enable these projects to
proceed. At the Grand Prairie campus alone, total tenant investment is expected to exceed $40
billion, with Provident funding the building shells while end users invest substantially more in
equipment and operations.

Provident is concerned that the PFP as proposed by Commission Staff could drive capital
and development to other locations outside of Texas. Large load interconnection rules should be
designed to enable responsible development of data centers, while ensuring that utilities recover
actual costs. Financial security obligations placed on interconnecting loads should enable serious

projects and discourage speculative ones, but without creating punitive financial barriers that could

Provident Comments - Page 2

 deter investment in Texas. Further, such obligations should be connected to actual grid costs and
not create windfalls for utilities that are disconnected to those costs. In these comments we address
three main topics: 1) establishing a two-step interconnection process; 2) ensuring financial security
requirements are reasonable and aligned with costs; and 3) managing the batch study and
interconnection queue.

COMMENTS
1. Provident recommends a two-step process for interconnection.

As a broad principle guiding the interconnection process, financial commitments should
follow information and outcomes, not precede them. With this in mind, Provident recommends
adopting a two-phase interconnection process. Step One should offer developers a quick
availability and feasibility assessment, while requiring only a minimal financial commitment. Step
Two would provide developers with a full interconnection study and in return require a reasonable
letter of credit (LOC) that is tied to actual study costs.

2. The proposed financial security requirements should be modified.

Provident opposes the financial security requirements as they are currently drafted in
Staff's PFP. First, the rule would require financial security in the amount of $100,000/MW, 80%
of which is non-refundable under any circumstances, with the sole exception of after a site has
been fully energized. This dollar amount appears to be arbitrary, is punitive in magnitude, and not
connected to actual study costs. As proposed, this punitive requirement, presumably intended to
“weed out” speculative projects, becomes instead a deterrent to investment in data center projects
in Texas.

Provident supports cost-based recovery mechanisms so that utilities can recover their actual

costs and opposes imposition of arbitrary fees. As we commented previously, a financial security

Provident Comments - Page 3

 range of $10,000-$15,000 per MW at the early study phase would be a more reasonable and
proportionate approach, with additional security layered in as system impacts, cost exposure, and
required facilities become better defined through the study process.!

Further, the proposed security appears to be a stacked requirement, duplicative of the
contribution in aid to construction (CIAC) funds required later in the process. Financial security
that is required to be posted should be linked to actual cost causation for the proposed projects,
with timing aligned to study outcomes and specific, identified upgrades needed to accommodate
such projects. Finally, Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) should return a developer’s
financial security once actual costs are recovered.

3. More clarity is needed regarding the batch process and managing the interconnection
queue.

Provident appreciates efforts underway to clarify how the queue will be managed,
including the batch study process being developed at ERCOT, but additional clarity is needed. In
particular, Provident recommends that care be taken to avoid erecting new entry barriers to projects
that are already well underway. To do so would be a perverse consequence of these proposed new
rules. It is important, therefore, to give weight to the timing of initial submission of projects in the
queue, and to recognize those projects with maturity that are demonstrated through inclusion in
ERCOT’s regional transmission planning process and through previously executed
interconnection agreements. ERCOT should also give weight to developer actions that support

grid reliability or long-term planning (e.g., land/ROW contributions for new infrastructure).

! Provident Inc. Comments on Staff Discussion Draft New 16 TAC §25.194, (Dec. 19, 2025) at 6.

Provident Comments - Page 4

 CONCLUSION

Provident appreciates the opportunity to submit these comments and respectfully requests

that the Commission publish a modified PFP consistent with these comments.

Respectfully submitted,

Provident Ini

10210 N. Central Expressway, Suite 300
Dallas, TX 75231

(214) 215-1203

jhawes(@provident.net

Signed March 4, 2026
